instagram.author: bytobyi
instagram.body:
@therealbinkytako @binkytako
I use Quad to make my first app, it's called Binky Block. It's currently on the App Store, and no, I'm not some ex-meta software engineer, I didn't work at Google, I studied filmmaking in college. I'd say that there are three things that go into making an app. The first is an idea, whether it's a proven concept that you want to put your own twist on, like my screen blocker app, or a completely new idea that connects people who like unicycles or something, I don't know. What you need to do is flesh out that idea and have a very strong vision for it. The stronger that vision, the more you're able to plan out the beginning, middle, and end, the more likely you are to see it through all the way. The second thing is just persistence. Chances are, you're not going to be able to just one shot an app with a single prompt. And so as you're going back and forth with these models, just stay persistent. If you encounter issues, just feed it right back into the system and ask how to troubleshoot it. You can figure anything out. All you need to do is be humble enough to ask the question. And then the last part is sharing it. And that's what creators do so well. Make videos, host events, get people together, and get users on your app. Because at the end of the day, whether you're sharing a piece of artwork or a piece of technology, it really wouldn't mean anything without an audience. Like this video and follow for more.

I'd say that there are three things that go into making an app. The first is an idea, whether it's a proven concept that you want to put your own twist on, like my screen blocker app, or a completely new idea that connects people who like unicycles or something, I don't know.
